title: Slack Spotify Integration: How to Set It Up (2026)
summary: Slack Spotify integration connects through built-in triggers and actions without code. Use HTTP requests for workflows the standard options don't support.
body_markdown:
## Activepieces Compared with Other Slack Spotify Connectors


Where Make's Spotify listing is mostly triggers, Activepieces' is mostly actions. Other tools connect Slack and Spotify too, but they split the work differently, and that decides which flows each one can build.


### When you need many Spotify workflow actions


Activepieces gives a flow 4 triggers and 41 actions through its[Spotify piece](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/spotify) , one of 750 integrations, so a flow that starts in Slack has plenty to do on the Spotify side.


Make, another no-code automation platform, lists the reverse for Spotify: 35 triggers and 4 actions.


When a flow starts in Slack, such as a mention or a reaction, and then does something in Spotify, it needs those actions: search, play, pause, set volume, add to a playlist.


Slack's side on[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) is balanced at 14 triggers and 29 actions, so both ends of the flow have room.


Choosing it comes down to five points: It's open source: the core is MIT-licensed, and the 750 integrations, **about 60% of them community-contributed** , are counted straight from the public monorepo on GitHub, which means community developers shape what gets integrated.


- You can self-host it with Docker or Kubernetes.
- The Community Edition is free.
- The docs state unlimited steps.
- Custom API Call covers anything the catalogue doesn't list.


Each of these removes a different limit. Self-hosting keeps tokens and message content on your own server, the free edition removes a licence line from the budget, and the unlimited-steps claim means a long chain won't be cut off.


Custom API Call is the escape hatch: when a Spotify endpoint has no named action, you send the request yourself.


### When Make suits Spotify to Slack workflows better


If the flow runs the other way, Spotify event in, Slack message out, Make's 35 triggers are the better match.


Activepieces' four Spotify triggers (playlist items changed, new saved track, new playlist item, new recently played track) cover the common cases, but Make gives you more starting points.


If you already pay for a hosted platform and have no interest in running a server, switching for one Slack-and-Spotify flow buys you little.


Check the trigger you need by name before you decide, because a catalogue count says nothing about whether your particular trigger exists.


Pick the Slack trigger first, then match it to one of the Spotify actions. Test that pair with a single real message before adding any further steps, and reach for the HTTP step only when the action you want isn't listed.
